transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-11
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Lucas Moretti (Redwood SE), Nina Rosario (Solstice VP Data), Ravi Kapoor (Solstice Cloud Infra), Asha Mehta (Solstice Security), Tom Ellis (Solstice ML Eng)

Summary:
Quick renewal check-in focused on capacity uplift, EU & APAC region enablement, and data sovereignty controls. Customer signaled intent to extend with an incremental commitment if we can meet a 30-day pilot for EU private endpoints + clear KMS/HSM integration notes. Cost vs latency tradeoffs discussed; Redwood to provide micro-benchmark and amended SOW.

Topics:
- Capacity uplift (monthly committed tokens + burst)
- EU private / VPC onboarding and APAC region timeline
- Security: SOC2, audit logs, KMS/HSM compatibility, data retention
- Pricing and procurement timelines
- Technical benchmark and canary plan

Action items (short list here repeated in metadata): see action_items field.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time today. Quick agenda — check status on renewal, confirm region needs, and run through security asks. Is that okay?
[00:10] Nina: Yes, sounds good. We're a little pressed on timing, we want a decision by end of month ideally.
[00:15] Maya: Totally understood. I'll keep this tight. Lucas, do you want to lead on the infra constraints they flagged last time?
[00:21] Lucas: Sure. I pulled the notes from last week's deep dive — two main items: EU private endpoints with KMS integration and a predictable latency SLA for their EU customers. Also they asked about APAC activation and how long that provisioning would take.
[00:32] Ravi: Right. For Solstice, a lot of our front-end is served out of Dublin and Singapore, so latency under 120ms median is important for a chunk of inference traffic. We can tolerate slightly higher for background jobs.
[00:42] Tom: And for the realtime suggestions path we need p99 under 250ms, ideally under 200. We're also considering quantized models for cost saving, but want to validate quality drop.
[00:52] Lucas: Good callout. We can run a micro-benchmark with dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) and a hosted fallback to compare p50/p95/p99 and tokens-per-dollar. That will show trade-offs for quantization plus batching.
[01:05] Nina: How long would that take? We need something we can show execs.
[01:09] Lucas: I can run a 24-hour continuous workload sim with representative prompt shapes. I'll produce a spreadsheet with latency percentiles and cost estimates. 24 hours should capture warm-cache behavior.
[01:19] Maya: Great. We'll include that result in the renewal packet. On the commercial side, we heard you were looking at a 20-30% uplift in committed tokens and adding EU and APAC regions. Is that still accurate?
[01:29] Nina: Yes, that's our ballpark. We have a pilot in EU to start with — about 3 nodes worth of capacity (estimated) — then expand. The tricky part is the legal side: data residency for EU customer records.
[01:40] Asha: Security here. We need to confirm whether Redwood stores KV cache or prefix caches long-term, and what encryption keys are used. We'd like KMS integration with our vendor (Thales). Also, SOC2 documentation and how audit logs are surfaced.
[01:54] Maya: Understood. We do not persist KV cache beyond the serving window by default, but I'll include a writeup. For KMS, we support customer-managed keys via standard APIs and we have HSM integrations — I'll attach the compatibility matrix — I believe Thales is supported but Lucas will confirm.
[02:09] Lucas: Quick note: on Private deployments we can bind to your KMS and rotate keys; for Hosted API we can bring-your-own-key for encryption-at-rest. I'll verify Thales HSM specifics and call out any caveats.
[02:21] Ravi: If we go Private in EU, what is the operational overhead? We prefer Redwood-manage but behind our VPC.
[02:27] Lucas: For Redwood Private (VPC), we provide a managed control plane but the data plane sits in your VPC. We help bootstrap instances, but you'll want cloud connectivity team involved for peering and routing. Typical provisioning is 2-4 weeks depending on approvals.
[02:40] Tom: Two to four weeks — that might stretch our timeline. Is there a faster way to get a pilot in EU?
[02:44] Maya: Yes — we can do a hosted EU model variant with IP whitelisting and KMS support as an interim. It gives you the region-located inference but with less setup time — usually a few days to enable region routing. We're up-front about control differences versus full VPC Private.
[02:58] Nina: That could work as a 30-day pilot while the Private path is provisioned. Execs want to see concrete numbers quickly.
[03:04] Maya: Perfect. We'll propose a two-phased approach in the SOW: Phase 1 — 30-day hosted EU pilot (KMS + whitelisting), Phase 2 — Private VPC activation if pilot metrics meet the bar.
[03:15] Asha: For the SOW I need explicit SLAs and data retention terms. Also an appendix for security docs.
[03:20] Maya: We'll include SLA targets and a security appendix. Lucas, can you assemble the security pack?
[03:25] Lucas: Yep — SOC2 report, encryption details, audit log examples, and the KMS compatibility table. I'll drop it to the shared folder.
[03:30] Nina: On pricing, can you give us a blended number for hosted vs dedicated? Our CFO wants an apples-to-apples to evaluate.
[03:36] Maya: We'll provide a blended model: committed token price for reserved capacity, then overage on hosted fallback. We'll also show tokens-per-dollar for quantized vs FP16 runs. We'll call out burst pricing separately.
[03:45] Ravi: Any incumbent competitors we should be aware of — like other vendors pitching region-residency?
[03:49] Tom: CloudEndpoints (they pitched earlier) — but their latency was spikier in our tests. Anthropic was mentioned by product as an alternative for model quality.
[03:57] Maya: Makes sense. We'll highlight the predictability and routing/fallback policies that help maintain availability during spikes.
[04:04] Nina: One procurement question — what does the billing cadence look like for a dedicated pool? Monthly invoicing or quarterly?
[04:10] Maya: Typically monthly invoices for committed capacity. We can discuss invoicing cadence in the contract; we support quarterly in some enterprise deals but it's negotiable.
[04:16] Asha: Also need to confirm log retention windows for audit trails — 90 days is our baseline right now, but we may need longer for compliance.
[04:24] Lucas: We can extend retention behind a log-archive add-on; I'll include options and associated costs.
[04:29] Maya: On timelines — if we lock in the pilot this week, Lucas can start the benchmark immediately and we can have results by Friday. SOW sent early next week, signature target by 2026-05-28. Does that work?
[04:40] Nina: Works from our side, procurement will try to accelerate but we'll confirm.
[04:43] Ravi: Quick technical question — about model pinning: if we roll forward to a quantized variant for cost, can we pin a revision so we don't get silent quality changes?
[04:51] Lucas: Yes, model version pinning is supported per-route. Rollouts can be canaryed, and we have automatic fallback to a higher-precision variant if quality regressions are detected. We'll show the rollout control screenshot in the packet.
[05:02] Tom: Nice. For canarying, can we run A/B with traffic split for 24 hours then roll back automatically if evals fail?
[05:08] Lucas: Exactly. You can set thresholds for automatic rollback based on eval metrics or latency/cost constraints.
[05:14] Maya: Anything else on the security side?
[05:16] Asha: Just one more: we require customer-managed key rotation schedule and proof of key deletion ability for decommission.
[05:24] Lucas: We'll document rotation APIs and key deletion processes in the security appendix.
[05:29] Maya: Great. Let's recap next steps — Lucas runs the micro-benchmark (24hrs), Maya sends SOW + security appendix and pricing, Solstice confirms procurement path and timeline. We'll reconvene after the benchmark and SOW — propose next check in 2026-05-18.
[05:43] Nina: 5/18 works.
[05:45] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invite and share the security pack link.
[05:50] (meeting closes, small chitchat)

Notes on transcription: There are a few places where names were automatically labeled as generic speaker tags; some words (e.g., "KV cache", "HSM/Thales") may be rendered slightly off in auto-captioning. Natural speech interruptions and clarifications present.
